header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #143: "Duplicate detection: flag pairs where both expenses already have a receipt".

## Problem

The expense duplicate detector (`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala`) recognizes two shapes, both requiring a survivor with a bank statement row:

- receipt shape: survivor has a row and no receipt; loser has no row and a receipt.
- orphan shape: survivor has a row; loser has neither a row nor a receipt.

A third shape is never flagged: the survivor has a row AND a receipt, and the loser has a receipt but no row.

This happens when the same purchase ticket is sent twice. Some retailers regenerate their e-ticket PDF on every download, so the bytes (and the sha256 the document dedup relies on) differ, the second upload is accepted, and it creates a new standalone expense. The bank-row expense already carries the first copy of the receipt, so neither existing shape matches and the duplicate silently inflates totals.

## Proposal

Add a third shape to `ExpenseDuplicateDetector`:

- receipt-on-both shape: survivor has a row and a receipt; loser has no row and a receipt.
- Same matching as today: exact amount, date within `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays`, Strong when both merchants are defined and equal, otherwise Weak; ambiguity counted across all shapes.

Resolution: the survivor can only hold one receipt (`receipt_expense_id_unique`), so the merge cannot move the loser's receipt. Instead it deletes the loser expense and discards the loser's receipt (refunds reassigned to the survivor, as in the orphan merge). The confirmation dialog must show both receipts so the user can verify they are the same ticket before confirming, since the action discards one.

DECISION on the open question (resolved by the maintainer, do NOT reopen it): discard the loser receipt by hard-deleting it and its underlying document, not by marking it ignored. Avoid clutter in the receipts list. Make sure the document/storage object is removed the same way other delete paths in this codebase remove a receipt and its document, and keep all deletes user-scoped (WHERE user_id = ?) and in the same transaction as the merge.

## Acceptance criteria

- A pair where the survivor has row + receipt and the loser has receipt + no row is returned as a candidate, with the correct tier and ambiguity flag.
- Strong + unambiguous candidates of this shape are bulk-eligible like the others.
- Resolving it removes the loser expense, hard-deletes the loser receipt and its document, reassigns refunds, and leaves the survivor and its receipt untouched.
- The UI distinguishes this shape (both receipts visible, wording says one receipt will be discarded).
- `ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec` covers the new shape, including mixed-shape ambiguity.

## Out of scope

Preventing the re-send at ingestion time (content-level dedup on merchant + amount + date instead of file hash) is a separate improvement. Do not implement it.

## Project conventions (must follow)

- All DB queries (reads and writes) include `WHERE user_id = ?`; list queries have `ORDER BY`.
- App-level validation only; no DB CHECK/DEFAULT for business rules.
- Use Chimney `transformInto` for case-class/sum-type shape mapping instead of manual field copying.
- No silent defaults for missing data: fail loudly.
- No external API calls in tests: testcontainers Postgres + fakes.
- Custom wart `NamedArguments`: when a call passes 2+ arguments of the same type, pass them by name.
- Add field-length/count limits on any new API surface.
- Comments explain intent, never narrate the change.

resultJson.description:
Issue #143: the expense duplicate detector misses a third duplicate shape. The survivor (bank-row expense) already has a receipt, and the loser (an expense with no row) has its own receipt. This happens when a retailer regenerates its e-ticket PDF, so the sha256 document dedup lets the second upload through and it creates a standalone expense that inflates totals. Neither existing shape matches it (receipt shape needs a survivor with no receipt; orphan shape needs a loser with no receipt), so the pair is never flagged.

The epic adds a "receipt-on-both" shape end to end. The web detector reports it with the same matching rules as the other shapes: exact amount, date within ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays, Strong only when both merchants are defined and equal, and ambiguity counted across all three shapes. Strong, unambiguous candidates of this shape can be bulk-merged like the others. The merge cannot move the loser's receipt because of the receipt_expense_id_unique constraint. Instead, in one user-scoped DB transaction it reassigns the loser's refunds to the survivor, deletes the loser expense, and hard-deletes the loser receipt's document row. The FK cascade on receipt.document_id removes the receipt row, and the cascade on telegram_receipt removes that row too. After the commit, the stored blob is deleted through BlobStorage, matching the existing receipt/document delete actions. The survivor, its receipt, and its details are left untouched, so only MergeDetailsSource.Row is valid for this shape. Per the maintainer's decision, the loser receipt is hard-deleted, not ignored; that decision is not open for discussion.

Hard-deleting a receipt cannot be undone. So the merge request carries the shape the user confirmed, and the server checks it against the current DB state before doing anything. If they differ (for example, the survivor gained a receipt after detection), the merge fails loudly and does not quietly switch from "move receipt" to "discard receipt". The UI shows this shape separately: the card and the confirm dialog show both receipts (each with a View receipt button), and the wording says one receipt will be discarded. Ingestion-time content dedup is out of scope.

tasks.title: Backend: receipt-on-both merge (discard loser receipt + document + blob) with explicit expected shape
tasks.description:
Goal: POST /expenses/:id/merge can resolve the receipt-on-both shape, and every merge request now states the shape the client expects.

1. lib/api/shared: add `MergeShape` enum in `net.wiringbits.api.models.expenses` (Receipt "receipt", Orphan "orphan", ReceiptOnBoth "receipt_on_both"). Build its Play Format and Tapir Schema the same way as MergeDetailsSource.scala. Add a required field `shape: MergeShape` to `MergeExpenses.Request`, with no default (project rule: no defaults on wire models). Update the scaladoc.
2. ExpensesRepository.merge, all inside the existing `database.withTransaction` plus the ConstraintViolations wrapper:
   - Add a `shape` param. In validateMerge/checkReceiptGuards, work out the actual shape from the loser receipt (ReceiptDAO.findByExpenseId(loserId, userId)) and the survivor receipt (ReceiptDAO.findByExpenseId(survivorId, userId)). Loser has no receipt → Orphan (any survivor). Loser has a receipt and survivor has none → Receipt. Both have one → ReceiptOnBoth. Fail with a new MergeError if the actual shape differs from the expected one. Suggested message: "The expenses changed since the duplicate was detected; refresh and try again". Replace or retire SurvivorWithReceipt as needed.
   - ReceiptOnBoth also needs keepDetailsFrom == Row (new MergeError, like OrphanDetailsNotSupported). The loser receipt must also have refundId == None; mirror DeleteReceiptAction and fail loudly if it does not.
   - ReceiptOnBoth execution: skip adoptLoserDetails and relinkReceipt. Call RefundDAO.reassignExpense, then ExpenseDAO.delete(loserId, userId). Then load the document with DocumentDAO.find(id = receipt.documentId, userId = userId); fail loudly if it is missing. Call DocumentDAO.delete(id, userId); the FK cascade deletes the receipt row and telegram_receipt. Every query is user-scoped.
   - Change the return type so the caller learns the discarded document's storageKey. For example, `Future[Option[String]]` or a small result case class, set only for ReceiptOnBoth.
3. MergeExpensesAction: inject `BlobStorage`. After the repository future succeeds, if a storage key came back and it is non-empty, call `blobStorage.delete(key)`. Blob deletion runs after the commit, so a rolled-back merge never loses the file. Let a blob failure propagate, as DeleteReceiptAction does. Pass `shape` from the controller (ExpensesController.merge) through the action.
4. Update the web call site so web still compiles. In ExpensesPage.requestMerge, pass `shape = if (c.receiptId.isDefined) MergeShape.Receipt else MergeShape.Orphan`; a later task replaces this.
5. Tests:
   - ExpensesRepositorySpec "merge": update existing calls to pass shape. Add cases for ReceiptOnBoth: the loser expense is gone; the loser receipt and its document are gone (repositories.receipts.find returns None, document find returns None); the loser's refunds are reassigned; the survivor's receipt, row, merchant, notes and splits are unchanged; the returned storage key is correct. Add rejection cases, each leaving everything unchanged: shape mismatch (receipt-shape request when the survivor has a receipt, and ReceiptOnBoth request when the survivor has none), keepDetailsFrom=Receipt with ReceiptOnBoth, and another user's ids.
   - ExpensesControllerSpec: add the `shape` arg to every existing MergeExpenses.Request. Add a receipt-on-both happy-path test. Bind a recording BlobStorage fake via `inject.bind[BlobStorage].toInstance(...)` in guiceApplicationBuilder overrides, and give createLinkedReceipt a storageKey param. Assert the loser document's key was deleted and the survivor's was not. Add a test showing a mismatched shape is rejected.
Verify: `sbt "testOnly *ExpensesRepositorySpec *ExpensesControllerSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Web: model duplicate candidate shape as an ADT (no behaviour change)
tasks.description:
Goal: give `ExpenseDuplicateDetector.Candidate` an explicit shape so the UI and merge request can tell the shapes apart. Results must stay exactly the same.

- In ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala, replace `receiptId: Option[UUID]` with `shape: Shape`. Shape is a Scala 3 enum: `Receipt(loserReceiptId: UUID)` and `Orphan`. Leave room for a third case. Keep detect's pairing, ordering, tier and ambiguity logic unchanged; pairsFor can carry a Shape instead of Option[UUID]. Update the object scaladoc.
- Add a mapping from Shape to the wire `MergeShape`, for example `def mergeShape(s: Shape): MergeShape` in the detector or ExpenseList. Use it in ExpensesPage.requestMerge in place of the temporary receiptId-based mapping.
- Update the consumers to match on shape: ExpenseList.withMergedReceipt (Receipt adds survivor -> loserReceiptId; Orphan adds nothing), mergeDialogLabels, mergeSummary, and ExpenseDuplicatesPanel.columns/card actions (loser title and View receipt button).
- Update ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec, ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec and ExpensesPageSpec to construct and assert `shape` in place of `receiptId`. Change no expectations beyond that.
Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec *ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec *ExpensesPageSpec"`. This task depends on the backend task because it needs MergeShape.

tasks.title: Web: detect and resolve the receipt-on-both shape
tasks.description:
Goal: candidates where the survivor has a row and a receipt and the loser has a receipt and no row are detected, shown, and mergeable.

- ExpenseDuplicateDetector: add `Shape.ReceiptOnBoth(survivorReceiptId: UUID, loserReceiptId: UUID)`. Pair survivors from `withRow.filter(_.receiptIds.nonEmpty)` with losers from `withoutRow` that have a receipt. Include these pairs in `pairs` so survivorCounts/loserCounts count ambiguity across all three shapes. Use the same tierFor and window. isBulkEligible stays the same, so Strong and unambiguous candidates qualify. Map the new shape to MergeShape.ReceiptOnBoth. Update the scaladoc to describe three shapes.
- ExpenseList helpers in ExpensesPage.scala: withMergedReceipt must NOT add the loser receipt to the survivor for ReceiptOnBoth, because the survivor already has its receipt and the loser's is deleted. mergeDialogLabels: a discard-oriented title and label such as ("Discard duplicate receipt?", "Discard"). mergeSummary must say that the bank-row expense keeps its receipt and details, the duplicate expense and its receipt (a copy of the same ticket) will be permanently deleted, refunds move to the bank-row expense, and the action cannot be undone. bulkMergeSummary must mention that duplicate receipts of expenses that already have one are discarded. Bulk merge already uses MergeDetailsSource.Row, which is the only valid source here.
- ExpenseDuplicatesPanel: columns must title both sides clearly, e.g. "Bank row (with receipt)" and "Duplicate receipt". The card shows two View receipt buttons ("View bank-row receipt" and "View duplicate receipt") using ReceiptFileViewer.openInNewTab and receiptFilenames. Show a single action, mergeButton("Delete duplicate and its receipt", MergeDetailsSource.Row), with no keep-receipt-details option. Add a short hint saying the user should check the two receipts are the same ticket. The confirm dialog in ExpensesPage reuses ExpenseDuplicatesPanel.columns. Make it show both receipts too, for example by extracting a `receiptButtons(c)` helper that both the card and the dialog render. That helper needs ctx/receiptFilenames/onError, so pass them in or define the dialog content inside the panel object.
- Tests:
   - ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec: cover the new shape for Strong, Weak, out-of-window, and different-amount pairs. Cover mixed-shape ambiguity: one loser that matches both a receipt-free survivor and a survivor with a receipt is ambiguous in both candidates; one survivor with a receipt that matches an orphan loser and a receipt loser is ambiguous. Check isBulkEligible for a Strong unambiguous ReceiptOnBoth. Confirm the existing receipt/orphan cases are unaffected.
   - ExpensesPageSpec: cover withMergedReceipt, mergeDialogLabels and mergeSummary for the new shape.
   - ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec: test that the card renders both receipt buttons and the discard wording, using jsdom + BrowserRouter per docs/guide/testing.md.
Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec *ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec *ExpensesPageSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/expenses/`: wire models shared by the server and Scala.js web.
  - `MergeExpenses.scala`: `Request(loserId: UUID, keepDetailsFrom: MergeDetailsSource)` and `Response()`, using Play Json.format and Tapir Schema.derived with SName.
  - `MergeDetailsSource.scala`: an enum with `entryName` (Row "row", Receipt "receipt"), a hand-written Format that fails on unknown values, and `Schema.string`. Copy this pattern for any new wire enum.
  - Endpoint: `ExpensesEndpoints.scala:70` (POST /expenses/:id/merge). Client: `ApiClient.mergeExpenses(survivorId, request)` at line 161.
- `server/`: Play. The chain is controller → action → repository → DAO (Anorm).
  - `server/src/main/scala/controllers/ExpensesController.scala` (merge at ~line 72) calls `MergeExpensesAction`.
  - `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/MergeExpensesAction.scala`: a thin wrapper that currently injects only ExpensesRepository.
  - `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/ExpensesRepository.scala`: `merge(survivorId, loserId, userId, keepDetailsFrom): Future[Unit]` runs everything in one `database.withTransaction`, wrapped in `ConstraintViolations.translating(ConstraintViolations.ReceiptExpenseIdUnique)`.
    - Helpers: `validateMerge` (returns `Either[MergeError, ValidatedMerge(survivor, loser, receipt: Option[Receipt])]`), `checkReceiptGuards`, `adoptLoserDetails`, `relinkReceipt`.
    - The companion `MergeError(message)` enum includes SelfMerge, ExpenseNotFound, SurvivorWithoutRow, LoserWithRow, SurvivorWithReceipt, OrphanDetailsNotSupported, AmountMismatch and LoserSplitsNotFullyAllocated.
    - Errors surface by throwing `new RuntimeException(e.message)` inside the transaction, which rolls it back. Controller tests assert with `error must include(message)`.
  - DAOs in `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/`:
    - `ReceiptDAO.findByExpenseId(expenseId, userId)`, `ReceiptDAO.find(id, userId)`
    - `DocumentDAO.find(id, userId): Option[Document]`
    - `DocumentDAO.delete(id, userId)`, which throws "Document not found" when 0 rows match
    - `ExpenseDAO.delete(id, userId)`
    - `RefundDAO.reassignExpense(fromExpenseId, toExpenseId, userId, now)`
    - `BankStatementRowDAO.existsForExpense(expenseId, userId)`
  - Model `repositories/models/Receipt.scala` has `documentId: UUID` and `refundId: Option[UUID]`. Document has `storageKey: String`, which can be "" for legacy or test rows.
- `web/`: Scala.js + Slinky + MUI.
  - `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala`: a pure function.
    - `detect(expenses: List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense]): List[Candidate]`
    - `Candidate(survivor, loser, receiptId: Option[UUID], tier: Tier, ambiguous: Boolean)`
    - `isBulkEligible` (Strong && !ambiguous) and the private `tierFor`
    - `pairsFor(survivors, losers)` groups losers by amount and filters by the window.
    - Ambiguity: the survivor id or loser id appears more than once across ALL pairs.
    - Sort: survivor date desc, survivor id, loser id.
    - `GetExpenses.Response.Expense` has id, amount, date, time, merchantId, merchantName, notes, splits, createdAt, `receiptIds: List[UUID]` and `rowIds: List[UUID]`.
  - `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpenseDuplicatesPanel.scala`:
    - The card shows a View receipt button through `ReceiptFileViewer.openInNewTab(props.ctx.api.client, receiptId, filename, props.onError)`, gated on `props.receiptFilenames.get(receiptId)`.
    - Merge buttons call `props.onMerge(c, MergeDetailsSource)`.
    - The public `columns(c, categories)` is reused by the confirm dialog in ExpensesPage.
  - `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpensesPage.scala`:
    - The `object ExpenseList` (around lines 125–222) holds pure helpers that ExpensesPageSpec tests: `withMergedReceipt` (optimistic local state adding the loser receipt to the survivor), `dismissKey`, `effectiveSelection`, `runBulkMerge`, `bulkMergeSummary`, `mergeDialogLabels`, `mergeSummary`.
    - The component builds `MergeExpenses.Request` in `requestMerge` (~line 336). Bulk merge always uses `MergeDetailsSource.Row`.
    - The merge confirm dialog is at ~line 1108.
- Tests:
  - `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/ExpensesRepositorySpec.scala`: the "merge" block (~line 455) uses the `mergeFixture()` helpers, `withRepositories()`, `createReceipt(user.id)` and `repositories.receipts.linkToExpense`.
  - `server/src/test/scala/controllers/ExpensesControllerSpec.scala`: the "POST /expenses/:id/merge" block (~line 436) uses the `linkToNewRow` and `createLinkedReceipt(userId, expenseId)` helpers. createLinkedReceipt builds the Document with `storageKey = ""` through ReceiptRepository.createWithDocument. guiceApplicationBuilder overrides bind EmailApi, ReCaptchaApi and TokenGenerator. Other specs bind `inject.bind[BlobStorage].toInstance(new NoOpBlobStorage())`.
  - For an in-memory BlobStorage fake, see `ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec.InMemoryBlobStorage`.
  - Web specs: `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec.scala` (helpers `expense(...hasRow, hasReceipt)`, `survivor`, `loser`, `orphan`), `.../components/pages/expenses/ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec.scala`, `.../ExpensesPageSpec.scala`.

## Non-obvious facts
- `BlobStorage` trait (`server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/BlobStorage.scala`): `put`, `exists`, `get`, `delete(storageKey): Future[Unit]`. Implementations are S3BlobStorage and NoOpBlobStorage. S3 delete is idempotent.
- Existing delete paths:
  - `DeleteReceiptAction`: finds the receipt (and refuses it if `refundId` is defined), finds the document, calls `documentsRepository.delete`, then `blobStorage.delete(doc.storageKey)`.
  - `DeleteDocumentAction`: skips the blob delete when storageKey is empty.
- The blob delete cannot join the DB transaction. Commit first, then delete the blob in the action; never delete the blob before the commit.
- FK cascades (evolutions/default/3.sql):
  - `receipt.document_id → document ON DELETE CASCADE`, so deleting the document deletes the receipt.
  - `telegram_receipt.receipt_id → receipt CASCADE`.
  - `receipt.expense_id → expense ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting the expense alone would leave a dangling unlinked receipt. You must delete the document explicitly.
  - `textract_job.document_id CASCADE`.
- Pending ProcessDocument background jobs reference document ids only inside their JSON payload, with no FK. Existing delete paths ignore this too.
- Before this epic, the survivor-has-receipt + loser-has-receipt pair is never detected, and the server rejects it with SurvivorWithReceipt.
- An expense never has more than one receipt (receipt_expense_id_unique), so `receiptIds.headOption` is that receipt.

## Conventions
- Every SQL statement is scoped with `user_id = ?`. List queries need ORDER BY.
- Validation lives in the app, never in DB CHECK/DEFAULT constraints.
- Fail loudly: throw or return Left. Never fabricate defaults.
- Wire models get new fields WITHOUT defaults.
- Use Chimney `transformInto` for shape mapping.
- NamedArguments wart: name arguments when a call passes 2+ args of the same type, e.g. `(id = …, userId = …)`.
- Comments explain intent; they don't narrate the change.
- Tests:
  - Use testcontainers Postgres and fakes; no external calls.
  - Don't write action-level tests that duplicate controller coverage.
  - JSON in tests is multi-line.
  - Test descriptions name the method only, not the type.
- Web:
  - Object-level `val`s hold only plain JS literals. Use `def` for reused React elements.
  - Component tests use jsdom + BrowserRouter.
- Verify with targeted runs only: `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` or `sbt "web/testOnly *Spec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Don't run the full `sbt test`.
- Memory notes:
  - Web tests need Node 24 on PATH; the default node is v16.
  - The full suite can OOM if another worktree is running sbt.
